framework: Cambridge International AS & A Level Information Technology (9626) syllabus 2025–2027
subject: Information Technology

outcomes.text: Distinguish data from information, since context and meaning turn data into information.
Compare direct and indirect data and judge their suitability for a purpose.
Describe sources of direct data: questionnaires, interviews, data logging and observation.
Describe sources of indirect data: weather, census, electoral register, third-party business data and published research.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of direct and indirect data.
Identify factors affecting information quality: accuracy, relevance, age, level of detail and completeness.
Explain why encryption is needed.
Compare symmetric and asymmetric encryption.
Explain the purpose of TLS/SSL and IPsec and their use in client-server communication.
Describe uses of encryption: protecting data and systems.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of different encryption methods and protocols.
Describe validation checks: presence, range, type, length, format, check digit, lookup, consistency and limit.
Describe verification methods: visual checking, double entry, parity check, checksum, hash total and control total.
Explain the difference between validation and verification and why both are needed.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of validation and verification.
Describe batch processing and its uses, such as bills, card accounts and customer accounts.
Explain master and transaction files in payroll and orders.
Describe the steps in sequentially updating a master file with a transaction file.
Describe online processing: electronic funds transfer, automatic stock control and electronic data interchange.
Describe business-to-business trading and online shopping steps.
Describe real-time systems where output affects input, such as greenhouses, heating, air conditioning, alarms, traffic and barriers.
Describe wireless sensor and actuator networks: smart homes, guidance systems and autonomous vehicles.
Write an algorithm for the steps of different processing methods.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of different processing methods.
Describe characteristics: longevity, reliability, availability, serviceability, security, MIPS and FLOPS, throughput and fault tolerance.
Describe their operating systems, number of processors and heat management.
Describe uses of mainframes: census, transaction processing and statistics.
Describe uses of supercomputers: weather forecasting, climate research and quantum mechanics.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of mainframes and supercomputers.
Describe the types and functions of compilers, interpreters, linkers, device drivers, operating systems and utilities.
Explain how a high-level language is translated for different systems using interpreters and cross compilers.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of different system software.
Explain the need for anti-virus, back-up, compression, defragmentation, formatting, file copying and deleting.
Describe file management, disk management and compression utilities.
Describe the uses of the different utilities.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of different utility software.
Describe uses of custom-written software by individuals and organisations.
Describe uses of off-the-shelf software.
Compare testing, support, cost and adaptability.
Distinguish proprietary from open-source software.
Describe command line, graphical, dialogue and gesture-based interfaces.
Describe the uses of each type.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each type.
Describe sensors: light/UV, temperature, pressure, humidity, pH, gas, sound, infrared, touch, magnetic field and proximity.
Describe uses in environmental monitoring, weather stations and patient monitoring.
Explain the importance of calibration.
Compare one-point, two-point and multipoint calibration and calibrate sensor readings.
Describe sensors in control uses: fluid levels, light, moisture, soil pH, gas, infrared and ultrasonic.
Describe induction loops, sound sensors and proximity sensors in smartphones.
Describe actuators and the movements they perform: linear, rotary, soft, hydraulic, pneumatic, electric, thermal, magnetic and mechanical.
Describe computer-controlled systems: greenhouses, heating, air conditioning, alarms, traffic, barriers and smart homes.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of control technologies.
Write an algorithm or flowchart for a control system.
Write and edit an algorithm showing decisions: branching, loops, nested loops and subroutines.
Write pseudocode using INPUT, WRITE, FOR, IF, WHILE, REPEAT and CASE.
Use comparison and arithmetic operators in pseudocode.
Draw a basic program flowchart to solve a problem.
Draw a decision-making flowchart with input/output, decisions, terminators, processes, subroutines, connectors and flowlines.
Edit a given flowchart.
Identify errors in an algorithm or flowchart.
Explain what personal data is.
Explain why and how personal data is kept confidential: removing geotags, anonymising, aggregating and duty of confidence.
Explain how personal data is kept secure, including network security.
Describe how unauthorised people gather data (smishing, vishing, phishing, pharming) and how firewalls help.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of methods preventing misuse.
Describe types of malware: trojans, worms, spyware, adware, rootkits, bots and ransomware.
Describe uses of malware: fraud, theft, espionage and sabotage.
Explain the consequences of malware for organisations and individuals.
Describe malware prevention software and physical prevention methods.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of prevention methods.
Explain what the digital divide is.
Explain its causes, such as computer performance and wireless connections.
Explain its effects, including unequal access and digital literacy teaching.
Identify the groups affected: age, city or rural, education, socioeconomic status, accessibility barriers and national development.
Explain how expert systems produce possible solutions.
Describe the components: user interface, inference engine, knowledge base, explanation system and knowledge base editor.
Describe scenarios: mineral prospecting, finance, insurance, fault diagnosis, medical diagnosis, routing and identification.
Explain forward and backward chaining with IF...THEN.
Explain data-driven and goal-driven reasoning in diagnosis, gaming and AI.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of expert systems.
Set up page structure for an audience or house style: orientation, size, fit to page, margins, headers and footers.
Insert, delete, hide, resize rows and columns and merge cells.
Control input with validation such as drop-down menus.
Protect cells, rows, columns, worksheets and workbooks, and freeze panes.
Create formulas using addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and indices.
Replicate formulas with absolute, relative and mixed references, including named cells and ranges.
Explain why each type of referencing is used.
Use calculation functions such as SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, INT, ROUND and SUBTOTAL.
Use counting functions and lookup functions such as VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, INDEX and MATCH.
Use decision functions such as IF, IFS, AND and OR, and date and time functions.
Use text functions, conditional functions like SUMIF, error trapping, nested functions and TRANSPOSE.
Use appropriate input and error messages.
Format cells for date, time, text, numbers, currency, percentages, fractions, orientation and alignment.
Format cell emphasis, including conditional formatting and comments.
Judge spreadsheet requirements for different audiences.
Create and apply a test plan for functions, validation rules and conditional formatting.
Choose normal, extreme and abnormal test data.
Extract data by searching with text, numbers, dates, Boolean operators, comparisons, contains, starts with and ends with.
Sort data ascending or descending on one or several columns.
Summarise data with pivot tables, pivot charts, subtotals and groups.
Import and export data in csv, txt and pdf form and as graphs and charts.
Create a chart suited to its purpose from contiguous, non-contiguous or specified data.
Create bar, pie, line, comparative and combination charts.
Format titles, legends, segment labels, values, percentages and axis labels.
Set axis scales, data intervals, a secondary axis and extract a pie sector.
Use what-if analysis: predict results, model scenarios and use goal seek.
Describe modelling uses: finance, population, climate, weather, queues, traffic and construction.
Describe the characteristics of modelling software and the need for computer models.
Judge the effectiveness of spreadsheet models.
Use models to run simulations such as disaster planning, pilot training, driving and nuclear research.
Assign data types and field sizes: text, alphanumeric, numeric, date, time and Boolean.
Describe one-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-many relationships.
Describe primary, compound, foreign and composite keys.
Explain referential integrity and its importance.
Distinguish a flat file from a relational database and say when each suits.
Create and use one-to-one and one-to-many relationships.
Create and interpret conceptual, logical and physical entity relationship diagrams.
Create a relational database and set key fields.
Validate and verify data entry and test validation rules.
Choose among static, dynamic, simple, complex, nested and summary queries.
Perform searches with single and multiple criteria, parameter queries and nested queries.
Use queries to remove duplicates, create tables, append, delete and update records.
Summarise data and use wildcards, Boolean operators and comparisons.
Calculate with calculated controls and fields, and sort on several criteria.
Design a data entry form: fonts, spacing, white space, radio buttons, drop-downs, controls and subforms.
Design, create and edit database reports, including grouped reports and calculated controls.
Create a switchboard or menu.
Import csv and txt data, and export tables, queries and reports.
Describe data in unnormalised, first, second and third normal form.
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of normalisation.
Normalise a database to 1NF, 2NF and 3NF.
Identify data types: text, numeric, percentage, date and time, and Boolean.
Describe the components of a data dictionary.
Create a data dictionary with suitable data types for a situation.
Describe file types and their uses.
Explain why generic file formats are needed.
Distinguish proprietary from open-source formats and why open formats matter.
Use indexed sequential and direct file access.
Compare hierarchical, network, object-oriented and relational database systems.
Describe the features and organisational uses of a management information system.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each database system.
Set aspect ratio, trim clips and splice clips together.
Add titles, subtitles, captions and scrolling credits with readable text.
Add fades, pan and zoom effects and transitions.
Extract, resize, crop and insert still images.
Add, edit or remove audio in a video clip.
Change speed and apply filters and colour correction.
Export video in MP4, AVI, MOV or WMV and compress to different resolutions for DVD, internet or mobile.
Explain how compression methods affect video quality.
Explain why typical video editing features are used.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of export formats.
Import and add tracks, normalise and trim audio and splice clips.
Fade, change speed and pitch, and add delay, echo and reverberation.
Convert stereo to mono, apply equalisation and filters and reduce noise.
Overdub, including voiceover.
Compress audio to different sample rates and export in MP3, MP4a, WAV or AAC.
Explain how and why typical audio editing features are used.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of export formats.
Explain how file size depends on sampling rate and resolution.
Explain how compression methods affect quality: containers, lossy and lossless.
Describe types, characteristics and uses of digital currencies.
Compare centralised systems like cards with decentralised systems like Bitcoin and mobile wallets.
Explain blockchains as distributed ledgers for cryptocurrencies.
Explain impacts and risks for individuals, businesses, governments and the global economy.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of different digital currencies.
Describe the data mining process and its six stages from business understanding to deployment.
Explain how and why data mining is used: security, surveillance, business, research, healthcare and social trends.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages, including ethical and privacy concerns.
Describe types of social networking: chat rooms, instant messaging, email and social media.
Describe uses by individuals, businesses, organisations and governments.
Explain impacts on individuals, businesses, organisations and governments.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of different platforms.

subtopics.title: The impact of IT on society

outcomes.text: Explain the impact of IT on sport, manufacturing, healthcare, education, banking and e-business.
Explain the impact on news, entertainment, home, government, politics, individuals and organisations.
Explain the impact on monitoring and surveillance for individuals, organisations and policing.
Describe delivery methods: computer-based training, online tutorials, networked courses, MOOCs and video-conferencing.
Explain the impact on motivation, achievement and autonomy.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each delivery method.
Describe new technologies: AI, augmented and virtual reality, robotics, translation, holography and 3D printing.
Describe wearable computing, blockchain, the Internet of Things, molecular storage and autonomous transport.
Explain impacts on individuals, organisations, healthcare and scientific research.
Explain environmental impacts: e-waste, recycling, power use, manufacturing and wireless energy.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each technology.
Describe LAN, WAN, client-server, peer-to-peer, VPN and mobile networks.
Describe their topologies, architecture and protocols.
Describe their uses: sharing resources and peripherals, BitTorrent, internet, tunnelling, telephony and content delivery.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each type.
Describe the role of network cards, repeaters, hubs, switches, access points, gateways, bridges and routers.
Explain how each component operates and works with the others.
Describe server types: file, web, mail, applications, print, FTP, proxy and virtual servers.
Explain the role of servers in a network.
Explain request-and-response communication between clients and servers, and server farms.
Judge the advantages and disadvantages of each server type for a scenario.
Describe cloud computing and its sharing of computing resources.
Describe uses by individuals and organisations.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of cloud computing.
Define bandwidth and bit rate and compare the bandwidth of different transmission media and access technologies.
Explain real-time and on-demand streaming and how bit rate and bandwidth affect it.
Describe the properties of fibre optic, coaxial and twisted pair cables, and lasers.
Describe typical applications of each method.
Explain how the medium limits bandwidth for data, streaming and ultra-high definition TV.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each method.
Define a protocol and explain why protocols are necessary.
Describe the purposes of TCP, IP, ICMP, ARP, DHCP and UDP.
Describe HTTP/HTTPS, FTP, tunnelling, SMTP, POP3, IMAP, Telnet, SSH, IPsec and TLS/SSL.
Describe packet switching, packet structure and connection and connectionless modes.
Describe circuit switching and message switching with store and forward.
Describe MAC and IP addressing, including IPv4 and IPv6.
Compare static and dynamic routing and the use of routing tables.
Describe the function of interior, exterior and border gateway protocols.
Describe the layers of TCP/IP and OSI and compare the two.
Explain how firewalls are used and configured to control network access.
Describe wireless transmission methods: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, infrared, microwave, radio and NFC.
Explain how they operate: data transfer, wireless protocols and wireless power transfer.
Describe uses: data exchange, mobile communications and the Internet of Things.
Explain wireless security issues, prevention and protocols such as WEP and WPA.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each method.
Describe the structure of cellular networks and the use of 3G, 4G and 5G.
Explain how satellite systems prepare, send and receive data.
Describe uses: GPS, global mapping, surveillance, telecommunications and ultra-high definition TV.
Describe threats: brute force, denial of service, botnets, malware, malicious actors, SQL injection and poor policies.
Explain impacts: data destruction, manipulation, theft and identity theft.
Describe physical measures: barriers, locks, surveillance, alarms and guards.
Describe software measures: biometrics, anti-malware, encryption and access rights.
Explain how firewalls are configured to control access.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of security methods.
Identify disasters causing data loss: natural, equipment and power failure, cybercrime, malware and accidents.
Explain risk analysis, perpetrator analysis, risk testing and quantifying risk.
Explain how to detect threats, prevent disasters and restore afterwards.
Describe strategies to minimise risk: power protection, passwords, malware protection and back-ups.

topics.title: 15.1 The stages of the project life cycle

outcomes.text: Describe project initiation: objectives, resources, success criteria, stakeholders, scope and schedule.
Describe project planning: detailed resources and task scheduling.
Describe execution and monitoring: implementing, tracking time, cost and quality, and reporting.
Describe project close and why reviews are done.
Describe types: desktop, web-based, mobile, personal, single-user and collaborative.
Describe uses: planning, scheduling, resources, costings, communication and collaboration.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of the types and of using such software.

topics.title: 15.3 Tools and techniques for project management tasks

outcomes.text: Create, use and interpret Gantt charts.
Create and interpret PERT charts, with tasks, timings, float, milestones, dependencies and deliverables.
Calculate the critical path and use it for work flow, costing and resources.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of Gantt, PERT and CPM.

topics.title: 16.1 The stages in the system life cycle

outcomes.text: Define a system as hardware, software or both.
Describe the stages of developing a system.
Explain how the stages relate.
Describe research methods: questionnaires, interviews, observation and document analysis.
Describe the content and purpose of user requirements, system and design specifications.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each research method.
Draw level 0, 1 and 2 data flow diagrams and system flowcharts with correct symbols.
Describe data storage in databases and input and output files.
Describe input forms: features, data collection, validation and input screen layouts.
Describe output reports: screen and printed layouts.
Explain why testing is needed, what a test plan contains and create one.
Describe the types and purpose of test data.
Distinguish alpha from beta testing.
Distinguish white box from black box testing.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of the types of testing.
Describe parallel running, direct changeover, phased and pilot implementation.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each and judge the suitability for a situation.
Describe requirements, design, technical, user and marketing documentation and why each is needed.
Describe the contents of each type.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each type.
Evaluate a new system for efficiency, ease of use and appropriateness.
Describe evaluation techniques: checking against specifications, user requirements and user feedback.
Describe the stages of agile, iterative, incremental, RAD and waterfall methods.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each method.
Describe evolutionary, incremental, throwaway and rapid prototyping and why each is needed.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each type.
Describe perfective, adaptive, preventive and corrective maintenance and why each is needed.
Explain how each type is carried out.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each type.
Transform and clean data to extract meaningful information.
Compare and consolidate data from two sources.
Split data into fields and merge data into required fields.
Display data with pivot table reports and pivot charts.
Explain when and why mail merge is used.
Explain the need for data sources and master documents.
Create, edit and use source data in suitable software.
Create master documents for letters, labels and directories.
Link a master document to a source file, using correct field names and embedding a chart or table.
Insert merge fields, document properties, document fields and date/time fields.
Set up manual fields (Fill-in and Ask) with prompts, and calculation fields with formulas.
Specify rules to select, sort, filter and exclude recipients.
Use conditional fields such as If Then Else, Skip Record If and Next Record If.
Use layer tools: add, remove, select, order, hide, lock, change opacity and merge or flatten.
Use transform tools: resize, skew, reflect, rotate, move, scale, shear, envelope and perspective.
Use grouping tools: group, ungroup, combine, add, subtract and intersect.
Use alignment, distribution and order tools.
Use layout tools: rulers, grids, guidelines and snapping.
Use colour picker and crop tools.
Explain RGB, HSL, CMYK and CMS colour systems and how they produce colour.
Explain image resolution needs and the effect of too low or too high resolution.
Choose bitmap or vector formats for a scenario and export as SVG, BMP, JPG, PNG, GIF, TIF or PDF.
Change solid and gradient fills.
Create a vector graphic to meet an application and audience.
Use drawing tools: freehand, Bezier curves, lines and shapes, with envelopes and perspective.
Use selection tools: convert to curves, replication and transformation, and solid and gradient fills.
Add, move and delete nodes to simplify paths and use Bezier handles.
Work with symmetrical, asymmetrical, cusp and smooth nodes and align nodes.
Convert bitmaps to vector shapes by tracing and weigh the advantages and disadvantages.
Create and edit bitmap images to meet an application and audience.
Use selection tools: lasso, magic wand, colour select, cut-out, crop and masks.
Work with colour: fills, black and white, greyscale, brightness, contrast, balance, shadows and highlights.
Use brush, pencil and pen tools with preset and customised options.
Use filters: distort, clone, erase, blur, smudge, sharpen and red-eye removal.
Resize image or canvas by changing colour depth and resolution.
Explain what compression is.
Compare lossless and lossy compression.
Explain the effects of compression on images.
Select font face, size, kerning, letter spacing and line spacing.
Fit text to a path or shape and set text in a shape.
Convert text to curves.
Use and manipulate text in graphics software.
Create stop-motion and key-frame animations to meet an application and audience.
Configure the stage: colour, size, aspect ratio, rulers, guides, grid and snapping.
Import and create vector objects, trace bitmaps and add text.
Control object properties: stroke, fill, size, position, orientation and transparency.
Set paths, use layers and masks, and control frame rates, looping and stopping.
Explain frames, key frames, property key frames, timings and coordinates.
Use tweening to change motion, shape, size and colour, and explain morphing.
Compare cel, stop motion, time lapse, flip book, CGI, 2D and 3D animation.
Describe the primary and secondary components of an animation, such as characters, sound and background.
Use animation variables to control the position of objects.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of the animation types.
Add interactivity to web pages by inserting JavaScript in HTML and using external scripts.
Change HTML content: text, numbers, calculations, string manipulation and images.
Change HTML styles and show or hide elements.
Display data with innerHTML, document.write, alert and console.log.
React to events: onload, onchange, onclick, onmouseover, onmouseout and onkeydown.
Provide interaction with confirm() and prompt().
Describe JavaScript syntax: literals, variables, operators, expressions, keywords and comments.
Write functions run by events, by calls or automatically.
Use timing events setTimeout and setInterval.
Use for, for/in, while and do/while loops.
Use data types, type conversion, variables and arrays.
Use logical, comparison and conditional operators including if, else and switch.
Use break, alert, prompt, confirm, functions and timing methods.
